name: Shearith Israel
note: The oldest Jewish congregation in North America; the only synagogue in New York until 1825.

name: B'nai Jeshurun
note: First Ashkenazic congregation in New York, formed by members leaving Shearith Israel. Host of the 1840 Damascus protest meeting.

name: Anshe Chesed
note: Formed largely by German, Dutch and Polish members of B'nai Jeshurun.

name: Emanu-El
note: Founded as a Cultus-Verein by German immigrants; became the flagship of Reform in New York.

name: Shaaray Tefila
note: Organized around Samuel Myer Isaacs, who led it for three decades.

name: Mikveh Israel
note: Pulpit of Isaac Leeser (1829–1850) and Sabato Morais (1851–1897).

name: Rodeph Shalom
note: Generally regarded as the oldest Ashkenazic congregation in the Western Hemisphere.

name: Keneseth Israel
note: Adopted Reform in the 1850s; David Einhorn served here 1861–1866.

name: Kahal Kadosh Beth Elohim
note: Site of the Reformed Society of Israelites (1824) and of the 1841 installation of an organ, which split the congregation.

name: Shearit Israel
note: Traditionalists who left Beth Elohim over the organ; reunited with the parent congregation after the Civil War.

name: Mickve Israel
note: Founded by Jews who arrived in Georgia in July 1733; reorganized in 1790.

name: Kahal Kadosh Beth Shalome
note: Isaac Leeser's first community in America (from 1824).

name: Jeshuat Israel (Touro Synagogue)
note: Building dedicated 1763. Without a resident congregation for most of the mid-century; maintained through bequests from Abraham and Judah Touro.

name: Baltimore Hebrew Congregation (Nidchei Israel)
note: Brought Abraham Rice, the first ordained rabbi to serve in the United States, in 1840.

name: Har Sinai
note: Often cited as the oldest continuously Reform congregation in the United States. David Einhorn's pulpit 1855–1861.

name: Oheb Shalom
note: Benjamin Szold served from 1859.

name: Washington Hebrew Congregation
note: Incorporated by an Act of Congress in 1856.

name: Bene Israel
note: First congregation west of the Alleghenies, founded largely by English Jews. Max Lilienthal served from 1855.

name: B'nai Yeshurun
note: German congregation; Isaac Mayer Wise's pulpit from 1854 until his death in 1900.

name: Beth El
note: First Jewish congregation in Michigan.

name: Kehilath Anshe Maariv
translation: Congregation of the People of the West
note: First congregation in Chicago.

name: Sinai Congregation
note: Grew out of the Jüdischer Reformverein (1858) led by Bernhard Felsenthal.

name: United Hebrew Congregation
note: First congregation west of the Mississippi.

name: Rodef Shalom
note: Successor to Shaaray Shamayim (c. 1847).

name: Ohabei Shalom
note: First congregation in Boston.

name: Mishkan Israel
note: First congregation in Connecticut.

name: Beth El
note: Isaac Mayer Wise's first American pulpit (1846–1850).

name: Anshe Emeth
note: Formed by Wise's supporters after his dismissal from Beth El in 1850.

name: Shangarai Chasset
note: First congregation in New Orleans; later merged with Nefutzot Yehudah to form Touro Synagogue (1881).

name: Nefutzot Yehudah
note: Portuguese-rite congregation; Judah Touro bought and refitted a church for its use.

name: Beth Israel
note: Grew out of the Hebrew Benevolent Association (1855); first congregation in Texas.

name: Emanu-El
note: Largely Bavarian and German membership; Levi Strauss was an early member.

name: Sherith Israel
note: Largely Polish and English membership.

name: Beth Israel
note: First congregation in Oregon.

name: Hebrew Benevolent Congregation
note: The 1872 return gives the founding year, a rented hall, and minister B. A. Bonnheim. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Shaari Chased
note: In 1872 the congregation had a building lot but no synagogue or minister. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Hebrew Benevolent Association
note: The 1872 return says it was organized 'two years ago'; the founding year is derived from that statement. It had a burial ground and a Sunday school but no synagogue. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Kehilath Bnai Sholom Ubikur Cholim
translation: Children of Peace and Visiting the Sick
note: The 1861 return dates the organization to 5 April 1855. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Bnai Yeshurun
note: The 1861 return gives 1851 as the year of organization. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Achduth Veshalom
note: The 1861 return dates the organization to October 1848. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Ahavas Achim
note: The 1872 return dates the organization to 1847. The congregation withdrew from the Board in May 1874. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Bnai Zion
note: The 1872 return dates the organization to 18 September 1853. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Hebrew congregation of Donaldsonville
note: The 1872 return says the congregation was reorganized in 1869; an earlier founding is implied but not dated. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Ohev Sholom
note: The 1872 return gives 1852 as the year of organization. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Beth Israel
note: The 1860 return dates the organization to 10 March 1860. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Bnai Zion
note: The 1872 return dates the organization to May 1854; the president acted as minister without salary. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Beth El (Hebrew Congregation of Los Angeles)
note: The 1861 return dates the organization to 2 September 1860. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Beth Israel
note: The 1860 return dates the organization to Tishri 5617 (autumn 1856). Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Shaare Shomaim
note: The 1861 return dates the organization to October 1856; the congregation could not support a minister. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Sherith Israel
note: Named in Board of Delegates survey evidence. Founding date and religious classification are not established by these returns.

name: B’nai Jeshurun
note: Named in Board of Delegates survey evidence. Founding date and religious classification are not established by these returns.

name: Adath Israel
note: Named in Board of Delegates survey evidence. Founding date and religious classification are not established by these returns.

name: Mishkan Israel
note: Named in Board of Delegates survey evidence. Founding date and religious classification are not established by these returns.

name: Beth Eil
note: Named in Board of Delegates survey evidence. Founding date and religious classification are not established by these returns.

name: Polish Congregation (survey description)
note: Named in Board of Delegates survey evidence. Founding date and religious classification are not established by these returns. The name is descriptive, not an established formal title.

name: Shaarei Tefillah
note: The 1861 schedule dates the organization to 1 May 1849; minister Rev. Isaac Hechinger. In 1877 the congregation told the Board it had never been a member. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Beth Jacob
note: The 1872 return dates the organization to November 1863; it had no synagogue building and a private Hebrew school. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Norfolk Hebrew and English Literary Institute
note: Reported to the Board as a congregation in 1860 under this name; organized 1847; minister Rev. I. Oppenheim. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Adereth El
note: The 1872 return gives 1853 as the year of organization; East 29th Street between 3rd and Lexington Avenues; minister Rev. Max Moll. The congregation resigned from the Board in April 1876. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Ahavath Chesed
note: The 1860 schedule dates the organization to 17 September 1848; 127 Columbia Street; 110 members. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Beth El
note: The 1861 schedule dates the organization to 8 August 1852; 33rd Street and 8th Avenue; 70 members. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Beth Elohim
note: The 1861 schedule gives 1859 as the year of organization, in Brooklyn's Eastern District; reader and teacher N. Gotthold. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Beth Israel Bikur Cholim
translation: House of Israel, Visiting the Sick
note: The 1861 schedule dates the organization to March 1855; 56 Chrystie Street; 150 members. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Bikur Cholim U'Kadisha
note: The 1860 schedule gives 15 July 1840 as the date of organization; Chrystie Street; 36 members. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: B'nai Israel
note: The 1861 schedule dates the organization to 5607–1847; corner of Stanton and Forsyth Streets; minister Rev. M. R. de Leeuw. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Shaari Zedek
note: The 1860 schedule gives 1840, the 1872 return 1842 / 5603; 38–40 Henry Street. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: B'nai Jeshurun
note: The 1872 return dates the organization to 24 April 1853; No. 9 Mulberry Street; president Nathan Barnert. The congregation withdrew from the Board in April 1878. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Beth El Emeth
translation: House of the God of Truth
note: The 1860 schedule and 1872 return date the organization to March (22 March) 1857, Adar 5617; Franklin Street. Isaac Leeser was its hazan and preacher in 1860; Rev. George Jacobs its minister in 1872. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Hebrew Society of Plaquemine
note: The 1860 schedule gives 1857 as the year of organization; ten members; no minister or school. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Sons of Israel (Bnai Israel)
note: The 1860 schedule dates the organization to 22 May 1855; eighteen members; hazan and shochet Lazarus Kantorowitz. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: K.K. Bnai Avrohum
note: The 1861 schedule gives 1856 as the year of organization; 26 members; Rev. Solomon Albu, chazan, lecturer and teacher. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.

name: Keneseth Israel
note: The 1860 schedule dates the organization to 5 October 5617 (1856); 39 members; Rev. M. L. Rosenberg, chazan and shochet. Rite and orientation are not stated in the Board of Delegates return and have not yet been established from other sources.
